what: The Online Stopwatch measures how long something takes, shown in minutes, seconds and hundredths of a second. You can pause it, resume it, record lap times and reset it.

It is useful for sports and running laps, timing a speech or a test answer, cooking steps, games, science experiments and checking how long a task really takes. It works on computers, tablets and phones with nothing to install.
It runs on your device’s own clock and nothing is sent to a server.
uses: Press “Lap” at the end of each lap to see each lap time and the running total.
Time your presentation and see if it fits the time limit.
Measure reaction times or how long a process takes, to 1/100 of a second.
Measure how long a task really takes, pausing while you take a break.
Time each round or each player’s answer.
tutorial: Click “Start” to begin. The big display counts up in the format minutes:seconds.hundredths, for example 00:12.47.
While it is running, click “Lap” to save a split. A table appears below with “Lap”, “Lap time” and “Total”. The newest lap is at the top.
Click “Pause” to stop the clock. The display freezes and the “Lap” button is greyed out while paused.
Click “Resume” to continue counting from where you paused. The paused time is not counted.
Click “Reset” to set the display back to 00:00.00, clear all laps and hide the lap table. The button changes back to “Start”.
features: The display shows time to 1/100 of a second.
After one hour, hours appear at the front, for example 01:05:30.25.
Each lap shows its own time and the total time since the start.
The latest lap is always at the top of the table, so you do not need to scroll.
Stop and continue without losing the time already measured.
Time is measured from the device’s precise clock, so it stays accurate even if the page is in a background tab.

example.title: Worked example: timing three running laps
example.text: Click “Start” as the runner sets off. At the end of the first lap the display reads 01:52.40, and you click “Lap”: row 1 shows a lap time of 01:52.40 and a total of 01:52.40. At the end of the second lap you click “Lap” at 03:47.15, so row 2 shows a lap time of 01:54.75 (03:47.15 minus 01:52.40) and a total of 03:47.15. After the third lap at 05:39.90, row 3 shows a lap time of 01:52.75. Click “Pause” to stop the clock, and read the table to see that lap 2 was the slowest.

tips: You cannot record a lap while paused. Click “Resume” first.
The “Total” column is the time on the main display at the moment you clicked “Lap”.
The time and laps are kept in this browser, so reloading the tab or coming back later carries on where you left off. Press Reset to clear them.
Human reaction time is about 0.2 seconds, so hundredths are only as good as your click.
On a phone, tap with the same finger each time for the most even lap times.
problems: It only works while the stopwatch is running. Click “Start” or “Resume” first.
“Reset” clears all laps. Write down or screenshot the table before you reset.
The time was lost after reopening the page
The stopwatch is saved in this browser only. A private window, a different browser or clearing site data starts from zero.
I want to keep the lap list
Select the table and copy it, or take a screenshot. There is no export button.
